results.name: Beyond testmetest: Native Addon Camouflage and 42 Armed GitHub Repositories Reveal a Hidden npm Publisher
results.description: Security researchers identified a sophisticated supply chain attack campaign involving 42 compromised GitHub repositories across 11 legitimate owners connected to the testmetest npm operation. The campaign evolved to use compiled native addons that decrypt hidden payloads at runtime, evading detection in CI environments through extensive anti-analysis checks. Attackers deployed polymorphic wrappers ranging from 12.9 to 13.7 MB that decode to identical publisher payloads, embedding execution hooks for AI coding assistants and IDEs. The operation included credential theft, repository hijacking, forged commit timelines, and automated malicious package publishing through GitHub Actions using npm trusted publishing. The infrastructure also links to shellpanel exploitation activities targeting cPanel systems. The campaign demonstrates advanced evasion techniques including environment detection for CI systems, containers, sandboxes, debuggers, and security tools before executing malicious code on developer workst...

results.name: ShinyHunters-Associated Vishing Group Linked to New INCEPTION Data Leak Site
results.description: A threat cluster designated O-UNC-053, previously linked to the ShinyHunters extortion crew, appears to have rebranded under the name INCEPTION. The group conducts voice phishing attacks to harvest credentials and bypass multi-factor authentication through social engineering tactics. Active since March 2026, the cluster targets multiple sectors including technology, healthcare, finance, and hospitality. Attackers use legal-themed phishing domains registered through providers like NiceNIC and NameSilo, with patterns such as legal-target.com. Over 70 specialized domains have been identified since October 2026. The phishing infrastructure mimics legitimate identity providers like Okta, filtering visitors to deliver targeted content. Stolen data previously appeared on ShinyHunters data leak site but now surfaces on the new INCEPTION platform. The group claims independence from ShinyHunters while acknowledging tactical inspiration from previous operations.

results.name: Volant Manticore: Flying Under the Radar
results.description: An Iran-nexus threat group named Volant Manticore has been conducting espionage operations since at least September 2025, with links to the Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS). The group shares tooling and tradecraft with MuddyWater but operates independently with custom implants including KuboShell backdoor and the Homa Framework. Cyprus represents the primary target focus, with operations against telecommunications companies and airlines, likely due to the island's strategic ties with Israel and Greece. In September 2026, coinciding with Saudi-Houthi hostilities, the group abruptly shifted to targeting Saudi Arabian healthcare organizations through intensified phishing campaigns. The operations employ sophisticated multi-stage infection chains, IPFS-based command-and-control infrastructure, and commercial RMM tools for persistent access. Attribution is based on tooling overlaps, shared infrastructure patterns, and operational tradecraft consistent with former MuddyWater operators now functioning...

results.name: Vinci RAT Delivered Through a Malicious Microsoft Store App
results.description: In early November 2026, investigators discovered an intrusion initiated through redirection to a fake snipping tool website, leading to installation of a malicious application called Setup Assistant from the Microsoft Store. This Electron-based application, published by ETPS Ltd and Microsoft-signed, functioned as a heavily obfuscated backdoor maintaining C2 communication and monitoring the victim's Downloads folder. The infection chain deployed a PowerShell-based remote access trojan named Vinci RAT, featuring extensive capabilities including host fingerprinting, security tool discovery, remote shell access, file delivery, and execution of various file types and shellcode. The campaign demonstrates sophisticated abuse of trusted software distribution channels combined with search-engine manipulation and fake download pages to establish persistent access.

results.name: Exposing the Gmail "Zero-Day" Behind Remus Stealer's Email Interception Feature
results.description: Developers of Remus Stealer promoted a new Gmail interception feature on November 8, 2026, claiming it exploited a zero-day vulnerability allowing mailbox access independent of stolen cookies, even after password changes and session revocations. Investigation revealed no actual Gmail vulnerability exists. Instead, the feature silently installs a malicious Chrome extension disguised as Google Sheets into victims' browsers. The extension leverages Gmail's Atom feed and attachment view endpoint to discover and download email content every minute, exfiltrating subjects, message text, and sender information to command-and-control servers. The technique manipulates Chrome's preferences files to register the extension and enable Developer Mode, using documented methods from previous research rather than novel exploits. Access persists only while victims remain signed into Gmail, terminating when sessions are revoked or users sign out.

results.name: ARTEX leads to persistent ZQAgent backdoor
results.description: NVISO has observed an increase in intrusions leveraging adversary LLM tools such as ARTEX. These LLM-driven attacks typically excel at exploitation and credential abuse, maintaining relatively consistent attack-chains that permit containment through isolation of initial-access vectors and credential revocation. Recently, NVISO identified ARTEX deploying ZQAgent, a novel backdoor providing long-lasting footholds within target environments. ZQAgent offers capabilities including arbitrary code execution, filesystem operations, and network tunneling. Observed in Belgium and Taiwan, all known samples connect to infrastructure associated with FOG0003, which has targeted government and human-rights organizations across Asia. The backdoor employs sophisticated evasion techniques including memory migration, process spoofing, and dual persistence mechanisms through systemd services and cron jobs. This deployment of persistent backdoors by LLM-driven tools represents a concerning evolution in autonomous attack capabi...

results.name: Recent Trends and Tactics of Agentic AI Attacks
results.description: Attackers are deploying autonomous AI agents in real-world campaigns, operating at machine speed and compressing attack lifecycles from weeks into hours. Between July and September 2026, over 10 global campaigns were identified targeting government, logistics, hospitality, manufacturing, agriculture and education sectors. Initial access was achieved through web shells on vulnerable web applications. The AI-driven operators matched skilled human tradecraft while executing hundreds of commands within minutes, demonstrating cross-platform fluency and adaptive reasoning. However, these agents left distinctive behavioral fingerprints including structured output formats, chain-of-thought reasoning comments, and section headers. The attacks leveraged open-source tools, demonstrated explicit security product awareness, and showed ability to pivot across Linux, Windows and multiple cloud platforms. Human operators provided strategic direction while AI agents executed tactical operations autonomously.

results.name: 13 Malicious NuGet Packages Target .NET Developers With Fake Job Assessments
results.description: Thirteen malicious NuGet packages were discovered targeting Windows .NET developers through fake job assessment projects. The operation began on npm in July 2024 and uses WinUI 3 and WPF button controls as lures. The packages employ multiple infection methods including MSBuild targets that download files after every build, DLL side-loading using Microsoft On-Screen Keyboard, and runtime triggers that download executables. The campaign hosts payloads on GitHub and uses various infection paths including trojanized wallet applications and ClickFix pages. The malware performs credential theft from Chrome profiles, implements GitHub repository-based command and control with embedded access tokens, and exfiltrates data to both GitHub and Telegram. Five distinct infection paths were identified, all connected through shared ownership, git identities, and embedded tokens.

results.name: Chaos Ransomware Profile: Tactics, Targets, and Indicators
results.description: Active since 2025, Chaos operates as a financially motivated ransomware-as-a-service group utilizing an affiliate model. Affiliates employ social engineering techniques, particularly spam campaigns and voice phishing impersonating IT support personnel, combined with legitimate remote-access tools to compromise target networks. Their extortion approach integrates multiple pressure tactics including data exfiltration, file encryption, threats to publish stolen information on leak sites, and distributed denial-of-service attacks. The group demonstrates opportunistic behavior, targeting organizations across diverse sectors and geographic regions that handle sensitive data or where operational disruption maximizes extortion leverage. Tracking indicates at least ten victim claims over two months, primarily affecting U.S.-based entities. Due to the decentralized affiliate structure, attack methodologies and indicators vary significantly between incidents, making uniform detection challenging.

results.name: IkonRAT: A Poisoned Update in the Supply Chain Compromise
results.description: In November 2026, a software supply chain compromise affected a legitimate business application used within the automotive industry. Threat actors inserted 6,438 bytes of malicious JavaScript into server.bundle.js, a document rendering component, delivering IkonRAT, a Node.js backdoor. The malware leverages the existing Node.js runtime to establish persistence, retrieve commands, and report results to attacker infrastructure at 45.61.163[.]206. Additional C2 tasking deployed payloads designed to bypass User Account Control and extract Windows credential material including SAM, SECURITY, and SYSTEM registry hives. The compromised component was distributed through the vendor's software distribution system, affecting multiple endpoints. Coordination with the software vendor led to identification and remediation of the affected component, highlighting the significant risks software supply chain attacks pose to organizations and managed service providers.
